Titre: Early detection of Xylella fastidiosa in olive orchards with UAV hyperspectral imagery and random forest
Resume: Hyperspectral images acquired by an unmanned aerial vehicle over 12 olive orchards were used to train a random forest model. Infected trees were confirmed by qPCR; overall accuracy reached 0.86 on an independent orchard.

Titre: Airborne thermal imagery and discriminant analysis for Verticillium wilt in olive
Resume: Airborne thermal and multispectral imagery were combined with linear discriminant analysis to classify Verticillium wilt severity in olive trees.

Titre: Deep learning detection of citrus greening from UAV multispectral images
Resume: A convolutional neural network was trained on UAV multispectral images to detect Huanglongbing in citrus groves.

Titre: Counting olive trees from UAV images with YOLO
Resume: We count individual olive trees in UAV orthomosaics with a YOLO detector and report precision and recall for crown detection.

Titre: Smartphone images and a CNN for olive peacock spot classification
Resume: A convolutional neural network classifies olive peacock spot disease from leaf photographs taken with a smartphone in the laboratory.

Titre: Twenty years of drought in olive groves from Sentinel-2 and Landsat NDVI
Resume: NDVI trends from Sentinel-2 and Landsat were analysed with Mann-Kendall tests to map drought in Moroccan olive groves.

Titre: Remote sensing and machine learning for olive diseases: a review
Resume: This review summarises UAV and satellite studies that apply machine learning to olive disease and water stress detection.

Titre: UAV and deep learning for olive disease monitoring
Resume: Book chapter describing UAV imagery and deep learning to monitor Xylella fastidiosa in olive groves.

Titre: Detección del estrés hídrico del olivo con drones y aprendizaje automático
Resume: Se utilizan imágenes térmicas de drones y random forest para estimar el estrés hídrico del olivo (olive water stress).

Titre: Olive water stress from UAV thermal imagery and leaf measurements
Resume: UAV thermal images and leaf water potential measured in the laboratory were compared; a classification of stressed and non-stressed olive trees is proposed.
